title: Internal Beta Activation Primer and Team Onboarding
content:
Purpose:
A concise primer to onboard internal teams (support, customer success, SRE, and early product partners) for an internal beta of a staged product feature. Focus is on day-zero readiness, telemetry and KPI collection, early feedback loops, and concrete escalation paths. This is intentionally lightweight so teams can copy sections into team-specific playbooks.

Audience:
- Product Ops (primary)
- Release engineers and SRE
- Support & CS triage leads
- A subset of product managers and solutions engineers running the beta

Beta scope summary:
- Cohort: internal employees + 10 trusted external early customers (up to ~120 users/day across regions)
- Feature surface: model-backed chat suggestion + routing to hosted/dedicated variants
- Duration: 3 weeks (rolling cohorts, week-by-week expansion)
- Goal: validate production telemetry, surface UX regressions, confirm autoscaling and fallback behavior

Pre-launch (T-minus 72–24 hours) checklist:
1) Technical gates (owner: Release Eng)
   - Deploy canary with traffic=5% to dedicated pool. Confirm KV cache warmup completes within 10 minutes.
   - Confirm telemetry tags included: beta_cohort, feature_flag_version, model_variant.
   - Smoke test: 50 scripted requests across sequence lengths 16/128/512; record p50/p95 latency and token-level error counts.
2) Observability (owner: Observability/Prod Ops)
   - Dashboards: "Beta Health" with panels for p50/p95 latency, error rate, token cost, request volume, prefix cache hit rate.
   - Alerts: page on error-rate > 1.5% sustained for 3m OR p95 latency > 2x baseline for 5m.
   - Logging: ensure sample responses captured (redact PII) and stored for 14 days.
3) Support & CS readiness (owner: CS lead)
   - Internal playbook created with triage steps and canned Slack/SMS messages.
   - Escalation roster published with phone/Slack fallback for on-call SRE.
4) Data & privacy (owner: Security & Compliance)
   - Confirm data retention and KMS settings for beta logs. External participants signed NDA (if applicable).

Day-zero launch script (first 8 hours)
- 09:00 Launch window open: enable cohort A (10% of internal beta users). Notify channels: #beta-coordination, #sre-oncall.
- 09:15 Run smoke script and share snapshot in Slack with p50/p95 and errors.
- 10:00 Manual UX pass by PMs on 5 live sessions. Capture 3 example transcripts per session.
- 12:00 Midday sync (15m): product-ops + release eng + observability. Decide expand/hold.
- 16:00 End-of-day recap with primary metrics and any high-priority actions.

KPIs to collect (primary and secondary):
- Primary:
  - Activation conversion: percentage of invited users who complete first successful interaction (target > 60% for internal cohort).
  - Mean tokens / session and tokens per successful response (used for cost baseline).
  - Availability: % successful responses excluding client-side failures (target >= 99.5%).
  - Median (p50) and tail (p95/p99) server-side latency for generation (targets: p50 < 200ms, p95 < 700ms for hosted; adjust for dedicated).
- Secondary:
  - Cache hit rate (prefix and KV): target > 40% within-hour after warmup.
  - Model fallback frequency: number of automatic fallbacks per 1000 requests (target < 2).
  - Human-reported quality regressions: count of user-submitted issues tagged "quality-regression"

Quantitative thresholds and automated decisions:
- Auto-scale trigger: request queue depth > 75% of capacity for 5m -> scale up 1 unit.
- Hold expansion threshold: sustained p95 latency > 1.5x baseline OR error-rate > 1% for 10m.
- Immediate rollback: any data exfiltration incident confirmed OR rate of 5xx errors > 5% sustained for 2m.

Feedback loop and experiments (owner: PM / Product Ops)
- Use short surveys inside the UI for first-session users (2 questions + optional comment).
- Maintain an "open issues" log in the shared doc with tags: severity, area (latency/quality/cost/UX), owner.
- Weekly lightweight quality gate: sample 40 responses and run evals against a fixed prompt set; flag any BLEU/ROUGE-style drops or manual quality flags.

Common triage flows (support):
- Symptom: Blank response or timeout -> check request traces, check fallback logs, verify model variant available; if transient, ask user to retry. If >3 occurrences for same user within 24h, escalate to SRE.
- Symptom: Hallucination/quality issue -> capture transcript, tag as "quality-regression" and route to applied-ml.
- Symptom: Cost spike -> check token distribution and batch sizes; if sudden, revert to conservative batching profile.

Sample Slack templates (copy + paste)
- Day-zero announcement (to #beta-coordination): "Cohort A enabled at 09:00 UTC. Smoke pass complete. p50=140ms p95=420ms error-rate=0.2%. Observability: <link>. Paging oncall if any alert fires."
- Customer-facing (for external early testers): "Thanks for joining the beta — if you hit anything odd please use this form: <link>. We're monitoring and will respond within 4 business hours."

Post-launch checklist (first 72 hours)
- 0–24h: Collect initial KPIs, stabilize flags, fix any blocking SRE issues.
- 24–72h: Expand to cohort B (+30% of internal testers) if no hold triggers occurred.
- End of week 1: Full metrics recap, highlight top 3 quality issues and mitigation plan, prioritize fixes for week 2.

Roles & contacts (minimal roster)
- Beta lead (product-ops): Sofia Rivera -> primary coordinator
- Release engineering owner: Ethan Miller -> deployment and rollback
- Observability owner: Daniel Kim -> dashboards & alerts
- CS triage lead: Priya Natarajan -> inbound support
- Applied ML contact: Dr. Lena Park -> quality regressions

Appendix 
- Quick checklist for copying into team playbooks: 1) Add cohort-specific contact + hours, 2) Confirm logging retention & PII redact, 3) Ensure sample transcripts are captured, 4) Subscribe required stakeholders to Beta Health dashboard.
- Decision ledger template: date, metric snapshot, action taken, owner, notes.

Notes and open questions:
- Do we want to include cost per-session alerts for internal only or also notify finance? (open)
- Should we auto-enable fallback to quantized variant after error spike > 1%? (ops/ML to decide)

This document is intended to be copy-pasted and adapted by team leads. Add items to the linked issues list and tag the document with any new lessons learned after each cohort expansion.
